correctness.rationale: The one-seed expectation equals 1+S_v/r by the deferred-edge exploration coupling and unordered connected-pair count. Cycle, path and rooted-vertex connection probabilities follow from two disjoint cycle arcs. Portal/mediator differences simplify to the displayed exact polynomial; a nonportal residual graph is the portal residual graph plus one edge, proving strict dominance. Descartes’ two-positive-root bound, together with endpoint signs at 0, 1 and infinity, proves exactly one physical crossover. The derivative at 1 and an O(r^4) second-derivative bound establish r^3(1-q_r)→6. 231 independently coded exact/numerical checks support but do not replace these all-r proofs.

originality.rationale: The exact physical crossover, all-vertex optimization, and cubic large-cycle switch are not implied by the closest investigated random-network site-bond vaccination threshold, small-world percolation theorem, or degree-normalized SIR vaccination heuristics. Searches of semantic result records and public literature found no equivalent or stronger implication. The unavailable complete 2022 source and unindexed niche work remain residual priority risks, not claims of exhaustive exclusion.
residual_risks: The full published article by Li–Zhao–Zhang (2022) was not accessible; its abstract is not evidence of whole-document absence of a relevant theorem.
An unidentified specialist result in finite-graph epidemic containment, reliability-polynomial ranking or targeted vaccination could have equivalent or stronger coverage.
The independent-bond epidemic coupling does not apply unchanged to general SIR models with correlated outgoing infections.

value.rationale: This natural two-community graph and optimal one-person vaccination decision has a non-obvious reversal: low transmissibility favors the degree-three portal whereas high transmissibility favors the degree-two intermediary. The exact all-r phase diagram and sharp r^-3 crossover are a structural planning insight and a nontrivial application of cycle reliability, graph containment and root counting; they are not a routine numerical gain, arbitrary invariant, or restatement of an existing general theorem.
